records.source: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ἐφέσῳ καὶ πιστοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·
records.gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God, to the holy [ones] the [ones] being in Ephesus and faithful in Christ Jesus:
pieces: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, to God's holy people in Ephesus, who are faithful in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.1: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus through [the] will of God, to the holy ones who are in Ephesus and faithful in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus:

R.1: This letter is from Paul. It was God's will that I should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. I am writing to God's holy people in Ephesus, who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in Ephesus"
alternatives: leave out "in Ephesus": "to the holy ones who are also faithful in Christ Jesus"
decisions.reason: Some of the earliest manuscripts, among them P46 and the first hands of Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have ἐν Ἐφέσῳ; almost all later manuscripts do. Without the place name the Greek is awkward ("to the holy ones who are and faithful"). The letter has no personal greetings and speaks of the readers' faith as something Paul has heard about (1:15; 3:2), so it may have been written for several churches in the province of Asia, with Ephesus as its chief city. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: apostle: a messenger sent out with the authority of the one who sends him
alternatives: a missionary or church worker in general
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:1: ἀπόστολος means one who is sent, and Paul counts himself among those commissioned by the risen Christ (1 Corinthians 15:7-9; Galatians 1:1). He holds the role "through the will of God".

decisions.choice: faithful: loyal and true to Christ; the same people as the holy ones
alternatives: a second, smaller group within the church
decisions.reason: πιστοῖς can mean "believing" or "faithful". "Holy" and "faithful" describe one group, the whole church, as in Colossians 1:2. The letter takes their faith for granted (1:15) and urges them to stay true (4:1; 6:10-13).

decisions.choice: Ephesus: the leading city of the Roman province of Asia, a port on the west coast of what is now Turkey
decisions.reason: The city was famous for its great temple of Artemis (Acts 19:27-35). Paul worked there for over two years (Acts 19:8-10; 20:31).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: God's holy people
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:2 and Philippians 1:1: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: It was God's will that I should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus; who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
alternatives: an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God; faithful in Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what an apostle is, as Colossians 1:1 does, and spells out "faithful in Christ Jesus": they are joined to him and loyal to him (m3).

records.heading: Greeting

records.source: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.
pieces: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.2: May God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} show you grace and give you peace.

decisions.choice: grace and peace: God's free kindness, and the wholeness and well-being he gives
alternatives: an ordinary letter greeting with no special weight
decisions.reason: Greek letters opened with a word of greeting from the same root as χάρις; Paul makes it a prayer for God's grace, and adds εἰρήνη, which stands for the Hebrew greeting shalom, the full well-being God gives. Both words return in the letter (2:5-8; 2:14-17).

decisions.choice: one source: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ together
alternatives: two separate sources of two separate gifts
decisions.reason: One preposition, ἀπὸ, governs both names, so the Father and the Lord Jesus are named together as the one source of grace and peace, as in Paul's other greetings (Romans 1:7; Philippians 1:2).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: May God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as Colossians 1:2 and Philippians 1:2 do.

records.source: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ εὐλογήσας ἡμᾶς ἐν πάσῃ εὐλογίᾳ πνευματικῇ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ἐν Χριστῷ, καθὼς ἐξελέξατο ἡμᾶς ἐν αὐτῷ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ, προορίσας ἡμᾶς εἰς υἱοθεσίαν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς αὐτόν, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἧς ἐχαρίτωσεν ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἠγαπημένῳ, ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν διὰ τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν παραπτωμάτων, κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἧς ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ φρονήσει γνωρίσας ἡμῖν τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν αὐτοῦ ἣν προέθετο ἐν αὐτῷ εἰς οἰκονομίαν τοῦ πληρώματος τῶν καιρῶν, ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ, τὰ ἐπὶ τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· ἐν αὐτῷ, ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἐκληρώθημεν προορισθέντες κατὰ πρόθεσιν τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐνεργοῦντος κατὰ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης αὐτοῦ τοὺς προηλπικότας ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ·
records.gloss: Blessed [be] the God and Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, the [one] having blessed us in every blessing spiritual in the heavenly [places] in Christ, \v 4 just as he chose us in him before [the] foundation of [the] world, to be us holy and blameless before him in love, \v 5 having predestined us to adoption-as-sons through Jesus Christ to him, according to the good pleasure of the will of him, \v 6 to [the] praise of [the] glory of the grace of him, which he graced us in the [one] having been loved, \v 7 in whom we have the redemption through the blood of him, the forgiveness of the trespasses, according to the riches of the grace of him, \v 8 which he made abound to us in all wisdom and insight, \v 9 having made known to us the mystery of the will of him, according to the good pleasure of him, which he purposed in him \v 10 for [the] administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up the all things in the Christ, the [things] on the heavens and the [things] on the earth; in him, \v 11 in whom also we were allotted, having been predestined according to [the] purpose of the [one] the all things working according to the counsel of the will of him, \v 12 for the to be us for [the] praise of glory of him, the [ones] having hoped-before in the Christ;
pieces: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. In {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has blessed us with every blessing the Spirit gives in the heavenly places.
Even before the world was founded, God chose us in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that we would be holy and without blemish before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in love.

He marked us out beforehand to be adopted as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own {{gender:sons and daughters|sons}} through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. That was what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gladly willed,
so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious grace would be praised, the grace {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has freely given us in the Beloved.
In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood we have redemption, the forgiveness of our wrongdoing. We have it because God's grace is so rich,
grace that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured out on us in abundance, with all wisdom and understanding.
He has made known to us the mystery of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, as it pleased {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to do. He set out this purpose in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}

as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan for when the times reach their fullness: to bring all things together under one head in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, things in heaven and things on earth, all in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we too have been claimed as God's own portion. We were marked out for this beforehand by the purpose of God, who works out everything as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will determines,
so that we who were the first to hope in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} would bring praise to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

L.3: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly [places] in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.4: just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose us in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before [the] foundation of [the] world, that we should be holy and blameless before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in love,
L.5: having predestined us for adoption as {{gender:sons and daughters|sons}} through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, according to the good pleasure of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will,
L.6: to [the] praise of [the] glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, with which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} graced us in the Beloved,
L.7: in whom we have the redemption through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, the forgiveness of trespasses, according to the riches of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace,
L.8: which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made abound toward us in all wisdom and insight,
L.9: having made known to us the mystery of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} good pleasure, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} purposed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
L.10: for [the] administration of the fullness of the times: to sum up all things in the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth, in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.11: in whom also we were made [God's] inheritance, having been predestined according to [the] purpose of the [one] who works all things according to the counsel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will,
L.12: so that we, who had first hoped in the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, should be to [the] praise of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory;

R.3: Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}! Because we are joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, God has blessed us with every blessing the Spirit brings, blessings from the heavenly world.
R.4: Even before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the world, God chose us to be joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He chose us to be holy and without fault in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sight, and to live in love.
R.5: Long ago God decided to adopt us through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own {{gender:sons and daughters|sons}}, with all the rights of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children. That is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted, and it gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} joy.
R.6: He did this so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious grace would be praised. He has given us this grace freely in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dearly loved Son.
R.7: Through the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son we have been set free, and our wrongs are forgiven. That is how rich God's grace is,
R.8: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured it out on us in full measure. He has given us all wisdom and understanding.
R.9: He has let us know the mystery of what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted to do: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plan, once hidden, now made known. God was glad to make this plan, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made it to be carried out through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.10: This is God's plan for the time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set: to bring everything in heaven and on earth together, with {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as head over them all.
R.11: Because we are joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, God has made us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} treasured share. He decided this long before. God makes everything happen the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned and willed.
R.12: He did this so that we, who were the first to put our hope in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, would bring praise to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: blessed be God: the Jewish form of praise that blesses God for what he has done
alternatives: a statement that God is blessed, with no call to praise
decisions.reason: Jewish prayer praised God with "Blessed be the Lord" (Psalm 41:14; 72:18), and Paul opens 2 Corinthians 1:3 the same way, as does 1 Peter 1:3. Paul plays on the word: Εὐλογητὸς, εὐλογήσας, εὐλογίᾳ. God is blessed (praised) because he has blessed his people. The Greek has no verb, so the line can be a wish ("blessed be") or a statement ("blessed is"); in this form of prayer the two come to the same thing.

decisions.choice: verses 3-14 are one long act of praise; the refrain "to the praise of his glory" marks its movements
decisions.reason: In Greek the praise runs from verse 3 to verse 14 as one sentence; the SBLGNT marks a pause at the end of verse 12, and this record follows it. The refrain comes three times (verses 6, 12 and 14): after the Father's choosing and adopting (verses 4-6), after the plan carried out in Christ (verses 7-12), and after the sealing with the Spirit (verses 13-14).

decisions.choice: spiritual: given by the Spirit
decisions.reason: Paul uses πνευματικῇ of what comes from the Spirit of God (1 Corinthians 2:13-15; Colossians 1:9), and the Spirit is named in verses 13-14 as the seal and pledge of these blessings.

decisions.choice: in the heavenly places: the realm of heaven, where Christ now reigns
decisions.reason: ἐπουρανίοις is an adjective with no noun; in this letter it always names a place: where Christ is seated (1:20), where believers are seated with him (2:6), and where the rulers and authorities are (3:10; 6:12). The blessings belong to that realm, where Christ already reigns.

decisions.choice: in Christ: through union with Christ
alternatives: by means of Christ only, as an instrument
decisions.reason: "In Christ", "in him" and "in whom" run through verses 3-14 about a dozen times. Every gift is given to those joined to Christ, and comes through what he has done; both ideas are present, and the second does not replace the first.

decisions.choice: God chose his people in Christ before he created the world
decisions.reason: ἐξελέξατο means God picked out a people for himself, as he chose Israel (Deuteronomy 7:6-8). His choice came before creation ("before the foundation of the world", as John 17:24) and was made "in him", in Christ. Its goal follows: a holy people.

decisions.choice: holy and blameless: set apart for God and without blemish, like an offering fit to bring to him
decisions.reason: ἀμώμους is the word for animals without defect, fit for sacrifice (Exodus 29:1; Leviticus 1:3). Paul uses the pair of people brought before God (5:27; Colossians 1:22).

decisions.choice: "in love" goes with verse 4: holy and blameless before him in love
alternatives: "in love" begins verse 5: "in love he predestined us"
decisions.reason: The Greek has no punctuation, and ἐν ἀγάπῃ can end verse 4 or begin verse 5. The SBLGNT puts it with verse 4: the holy life God chose his people for is a life of love (compare 3:17; 4:2; 5:2). Read with verse 5, it would be God's love that moved him to adopt them. Both are true; the question is only which Paul says here.

decisions.choice: predestined: decided beforehand, marked out in advance for a goal
decisions.reason: προορίσας is made of "before" and "to mark out a boundary". The goal is named each time: adoption (verse 5), and bringing praise to God's glory (verses 11-12). Paul plays on the root again in verses 9 and 11 ("he purposed", "purpose").

decisions.choice: adoption as sons: being made God's children and heirs, with the full rights of a son
decisions.reason: υἱοθεσίαν is the legal term for adoption (Romans 8:15; Galatians 4:5). Under Roman law an adopted son took the family name and became his father's heir with full rights; the inheritance follows in verses 11 and 14. Women and men alike are meant: Paul quotes God's promise "you shall be my sons and daughters" (2 Corinthians 6:18) and says that in Christ there is neither male nor female (Galatians 3:26-29).

decisions.choice: to himself: God adopts them into his own family
decisions.reason: αὐτόν most naturally refers back to the subject, God the Father, who adopts them as his own children through Jesus Christ.

decisions.choice: the good pleasure of his will: what God freely chose and took delight in
decisions.reason: εὐδοκίαν is goodwill or delight. God was not forced to adopt his people or to reveal his plan; he willed it and was glad to do it. The phrase returns in verse 9, and "the counsel of his will" in verse 11.

decisions.choice: the glory of his grace: his glorious grace, which he freely gave
decisions.reason: Greek often uses "X of Y" to describe: "the glory of his grace" is his glorious grace. ἐχαρίτωσεν is a verb from the same root as χάριτος: literally God "graced" his people, gave them his grace as a free gift (Luke 1:28 is the only other place it is used in the New Testament).

decisions.choice: the Beloved: a title for Christ, the one God loves
alternatives: any loved one, with no title intended
decisions.reason: ἠγαπημένῳ is a passive participle, "the one who has been loved". God calls Jesus his beloved Son at his baptism (Mark 1:11), and Colossians 1:13 speaks of "the Son of his love". In the Greek Old Testament the same word is used of Israel as God's loved people (Deuteronomy 33:5, 26; Isaiah 44:2), so it may also present Christ as the one in whom God's love for his people is gathered up.

decisions.choice: redemption: release, as of a slave or captive, at a cost; here, the forgiveness of trespasses, won by Christ's death
alternatives: a general deliverance with no idea of cost
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσιν was used for setting a slave or prisoner free by payment of a price. Here the cost is Christ's blood, his violent death given as a sacrifice, and the release is explained as ἄφεσιν, the forgiveness of παραπτωμάτων, wrong steps. Colossians 1:14 says the same without "through his blood"; Ephesians 1:14 and 4:30 look forward to the final day of redemption.

decisions.choice: with all wisdom and insight: the grace God poured out brought his people all wisdom and understanding
alternatives: God acted with all wisdom and insight in pouring out his grace
with all wisdom and insight he made known the mystery (verse 9)
decisions.reason: ἐν φρονήσει could describe God's own wisdom or the wisdom given to his people. Paul elsewhere uses such words of what believers receive (Colossians 1:9), prays in verse 17 for the Spirit of wisdom, and the next words tell what they have come to know: the mystery of God's will. Since God himself is plainly wise, the difference is small.

decisions.choice: mystery: God's plan, hidden until he reveals it
decisions.reason: μυστήριον in Paul is not something hard to understand but something God kept hidden and has now made known (3:3-9; Colossians 1:26-27). Here its content follows in verse 10: all things brought together in Christ.

decisions.choice: a plan for the fullness of the times: God's ordering of history, carried out when the time he set has fully come
alternatives: a stewardship given to Paul (as in 3:2)
a final age only, not yet begun
decisions.reason: οἰκονομίαν is the management of a household, then any plan or ordering of affairs. Here the manager is God, and the plan concerns history reaching its full measure (compare Galatians 4:4, where "the fullness of the time" came when God sent his Son). The plan is already under way in Christ and moves toward its completion.

decisions.choice: to bring all things together into one in Christ, under him as head
alternatives: to sum up, as an argument is summed up
to restore all things to what they were
decisions.reason: ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι comes from the word for a main point or summary; Paul uses it in Romans 13:9 of the commandments summed up in one. Here all things, in heaven and on earth, are brought together into one whole in Christ. The word sounds like the word for "head", and Paul goes on to call Christ "head over all things" (1:22), so the thought of gathering everything under him as head is close at hand. How fully the word itself carries that sense is debated.

decisions.choice: we were made God's own portion, his inheritance
alternatives: we received an inheritance, a share
we were chosen by lot, appointed
decisions.reason: ἐκληρώθημεν is a passive verb from the word for a lot or share. It can mean that God's people were given their share, or that they were made God's own share, as Israel was "the Lord's portion" (Deuteronomy 32:9). The second fits the passive form and the letter's own words: God's "inheritance in the holy ones" (1:18) and his "possession" (1:14). Colossians 1:12 speaks of believers' share in the inheritance, which is the other side of the same truth.

decisions.choice: "we who first hoped in the Christ": Paul and his fellow Jewish believers, who hoped in the Messiah before the Gentile readers did; "you also" in verse 13 turns to the Gentiles
alternatives: "we" is all believers, who hope in Christ ahead of the final day of redemption
"we" is the first generation of believers, Jewish and Gentile
decisions.reason: προηλπικότας means "having hoped beforehand". Through verses 3-10 "we" means all believers. But here Paul says "we" hoped first, in "the Christ", with the article, the Messiah Israel awaited, and verse 13 begins καὶ ὑμεῖς, "you also". Chapter 2 is about Gentiles and Jews brought into one people (2:11-22). On the other reading, "beforehand" means before the hope is fulfilled, and there is no contrast between two groups. Either way verse 14 ends with "our inheritance", shared by all.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), with "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}" where the Greek has the article; {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. In verse 12 the article and the hope of Israel point toward the title "Messiah" (m21); the setting lets readers choose.

decisions.choice: adoption as {{gender:sons and daughters|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word means adoption as a son, with an heir's rights (m10), and women are included. "Children" would lose the heir's standing that the word carries; "sons and daughters" keeps it and is Paul's own phrase (2 Corinthians 6:18). "Sons" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: God chose us in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; He set out this purpose in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; the purpose of God
alternatives: he chose us in him; which he purposed in him; the purpose of the one who works all things
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God and Christ where the Greek has only "he" and "him", since in English the two pronouns side by side would be unclear.

decisions.choice: every blessing the Spirit gives (B); every blessing the Spirit brings (R)
decisions.reason: "Spiritual" in current English often means inward or religious; Balanced and Readable say whose gift these blessings are (m3).

decisions.choice: blessings from the heavenly world
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer phrase from the Ephesians word list; the sense is the realm where Christ reigns (m4).

decisions.choice: Because we are joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}; God chose us to be joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable explains "in Christ" as being joined to him (m5). "Because" states the link that "in Christ" implies here: the blessings come to those who belong to him.

decisions.choice: with all the rights of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children
alternatives: as his own sons and daughters
decisions.reason: Readable says what adoption meant in Paul's world: full standing as an heir (m10).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dearly loved Son
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the Beloved" is (m14) and uses "dearly loved" from the Ephesians word list.

decisions.choice: we have been set free
decisions.reason: "Redemption" is church language for many readers; Readable says what it means (m15), as Colossians 1:14 does.

decisions.choice: our wrongdoing (B); our wrongs (R)
decisions.reason: παραπτωμάτων means false steps, wrong acts. "Trespass" now usually means entering someone's land; "wrongdoing" keeps the sense of wrong deeds. Literal keeps "trespasses".

decisions.choice: claimed as God's own portion (B); {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} treasured share (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m20. Literal says "made [God's] inheritance".

decisions.choice: Praise the God and Father
alternatives: Blessed be the God and Father
decisions.reason: "Blessed be" is no longer everyday English; Readable says what it means: a call to praise God (m1).

decisions.choice: to bring all things together under one head
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both parts of the sense chosen in m19: gathering into one, with Christ as head.

records.heading: Chosen, redeemed and sealed in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}

records.source: ἐν ᾧ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς σωτηρίας ὑμῶν, ἐν ᾧ καὶ πιστεύσαντες ἐσφραγίσθητε τῷ πνεύματι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῷ ἁγίῳ, ὅ ἐστιν ἀρραβὼν τῆς κληρονομίας ἡμῶν, εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῆς περιποιήσεως, εἰς ἔπαινον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: In whom also you, having heard the word of the truth, the gospel of the salvation of you, in whom also having believed you were sealed with the Spirit of the promise the Holy, \v 14 which is [the] pledge of the inheritance of us, for [the] redemption of the possession, for [the] praise of the glory of him.
pieces: And you also are in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You heard the message of truth, the gospel that brings you salvation, and you believed; and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you were sealed with the Holy Spirit God had promised.
The Spirit is the down payment on our inheritance, until God redeems those who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own possession, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory will be praised.

L.13: In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you also, having heard the word of the truth, the gospel of your salvation, in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise,
L.14: who is [the] down payment of our inheritance, for [the] redemption of [God's own] possession, to [the] praise of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

R.13: You also are joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. You heard the message of truth, the good news that God saves you. When you believed it, God put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seal on you: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave you the Holy Spirit {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised. This seal shows that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.14: The Spirit is like a first payment that guarantees the rest. God will give us everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised. The day is coming when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set free completely the people who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory will be praised.

decisions.choice: the praise of verses 3-12 goes on: "in whom" is Christ, and the refrain closes it a third time
alternatives: a new sentence with a new subject
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks a pause after verse 12, but ἐν ᾧ picks up "in the Christ" from the end of verse 12, and "to the praise of his glory" ends the whole passage as it ended verses 6 and 12.

decisions.choice: "you also": the Gentile readers, who have come to share what "we" have; "our inheritance" joins both
alternatives: "you" and "we" are the same people, with no contrast
decisions.reason: καὶ ὑμεῖς sets the readers beside the "we" of verses 11-12 (see the note there). Verse 14 then speaks of "our" inheritance, which Jews and Gentiles share alike, as 2:11-22 and 3:6 say at length.

decisions.choice: the sentence starts again with a second "in whom"; the main verb is "you were sealed"
alternatives: "having believed in him" (Christ as the one believed in)
decisions.reason: After ὑμεῖς ἀκούσαντες the sentence breaks off and resumes with ἐν ᾧ. The main verb, ἐσφραγίσθητε, comes only here: in Christ, when they believed, they were sealed.

decisions.choice: the word of the truth is the gospel that brings their salvation
alternatives: a true word that belongs to the gospel
decisions.reason: The two phrases describe one message, as in Colossians 1:5: the message is the truth, and that message is the gospel that saves them.

decisions.choice: sealed: marked as God's own and kept safe
decisions.reason: A seal pressed in wax marked a document or goods as belonging to their owner and kept them from tampering. ἐσφραγίσθητε says God has marked believers as his by giving them the Spirit (4:30; 2 Corinthians 1:22).

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the promise: the Holy Spirit whom God promised through the prophets and through Jesus
decisions.reason: God promised to pour out his Spirit and put it within his people (Joel 2:28-29; Ezekiel 36:26-27); Jesus spoke of "the promise of the Father" (Acts 1:4; 2:33), and Paul says the Gentiles too receive the promised Spirit through faith (Galatians 3:14).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: ὅ, a neuter "which", agreeing with "Spirit"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ between the neuter and the masculine form of the relative pronoun. Both refer to the Holy Spirit, and the meaning does not change. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: down payment: a first installment that guarantees the full payment will follow
alternatives: a pledge given as security and later returned
decisions.reason: ἀρραβὼν is a trade word, borrowed from Hebrew, for money paid at the start of a deal to bind the buyer to pay the rest. The Spirit is both part of the inheritance, already given, and God's guarantee that the rest will come (2 Corinthians 1:22; 5:5).

decisions.choice: the redemption of God's own possession: the day God sets his people fully free
alternatives: until we take possession of our inheritance
decisions.reason: περιποιήσεως means something acquired and kept as one's own. In the Old Testament God's people are his treasured possession (Exodus 19:5), and the Greek Old Testament uses this word for them in Malachi 3:17, and 1 Peter 2:9 calls the church "a people for his possession". It could instead mean the believers' coming into possession of the inheritance. Either way, the redemption here is the final one, still ahead (4:30).

decisions.choice: who
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the Holy Spirit; English does not call the Spirit "which" or "it", whatever the Greek gender of the word.

decisions.choice: down payment
decisions.reason: "Down payment" keeps the trade picture and its point: part now, the rest to come (m8). "Guarantee" keeps only the second half; "deposit" can suggest money that will be returned.

decisions.choice: This seal shows that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; a first payment that guarantees the rest. God will give us everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised
alternatives: you were sealed; the down payment on our inheritance
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures, the seal (m5) and the down payment (m8), and says what "our inheritance" is, using the wording of the Ephesians word list.

decisions.choice: until God redeems those who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own possession (B); when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will set free completely the people who are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own (R)
alternatives: for the redemption of the possession
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m9. Readable uses "set free" for redemption, as in verse 7.

decisions.choice: You also are joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ and explains "in him", as in verses 3-12.

records.source: Διὰ τοῦτο κἀγώ, ἀκούσας τὴν καθ’ ὑμᾶς πίστιν ἐν τῷ κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τὴν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους, οὐ παύομαι εὐχαριστῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν μνείαν ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, ἵνα ὁ θεὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ πατὴρ τῆς δόξης, δώῃ ὑμῖν πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως ἐν ἐπιγνώσει αὐτοῦ, πεφωτισμένους τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εἰδέναι ὑμᾶς τίς ἐστιν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς κλήσεως αὐτοῦ, τίς ὁ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης τῆς κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις, καὶ τί τὸ ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ κράτους τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ ἣν ἐνήργηκεν ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ ἐγείρας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ καθίσας ἐν δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας καὶ δυνάμεως καὶ κυριότητος καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματος ὀνομαζομένου οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι·
records.gloss: Because of this I also, having heard of the among you faith in the Lord Jesus and the love the [love] toward all the holy [ones], \v 16 do not cease giving thanks for you, mention making at the prayers of me, \v 17 that the God of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, the Father of the glory, may give to you [a] spirit of wisdom and revelation in knowledge of him, \v 18 having been enlightened the eyes of the heart of you, for the to know you what is the hope of the calling of him, what the riches of the glory of the inheritance of him in the holy [ones], \v 19 and what the surpassing greatness of the power of him toward us the [ones] believing according to the working of the might of the strength of him, \v 20 which he worked in the Christ, having raised him from [the] dead and having seated [him] at [the] right [hand] of him in the heavenly [places], \v 21 above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name being named, not only in the age this but also in the [one] coming;
pieces: For this reason, since I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all God's holy people,
I have never stopped thanking God for you. I mention you whenever I pray,
asking the God of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Father of glory, to give you the Spirit who brings wisdom and revelation as you come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

With the eyes of your heart opened to the light, you will know what hope {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} call holds out to you, how rich and glorious an inheritance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people,
and how far beyond all measure is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power at work for us who believe. It is the working of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty strength,

which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put to work in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead and set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand in the heavenly places,
high above every ruler and authority, every power and dominion, and every name that can be named, not only in this age but in the age to come as well.

L.15: Because of this I also, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus [that is] among you and the love [you have] for all the holy ones,
L.16: do not stop giving thanks for you, making mention [of you] in my prayers,
L.17: that the God of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Father of glory, may give you [the] Spirit of wisdom and revelation in [the] knowledge of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.18: the eyes of your heart having been enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} calling, what [are] the riches of the glory of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance in the holy ones,
L.19: and what [is] the surpassing greatness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength,
L.20: which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} worked in the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, having raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from [the] dead and seated [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right [hand] in the heavenly [places],
L.21: far above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the [one] to come;

R.15: That is why, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all of God's people,
R.16: I have not stopped thanking God for you. I keep remembering you when I pray.
R.17: I ask the God of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the glorious Father, to give you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, who makes you wise and shows you what God is like, so that you will truly know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.18: I ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to open the eyes of your heart and fill them with light, so that you will understand three things. You will know the hope {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave you when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you. You will know how glorious and precious {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people are to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: they are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own treasured inheritance.
R.19: And you will know how great {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power is for us who believe. Nothing can compare with it. It is the same mighty strength
R.20: that God used when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from the dead. God gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the place of honor at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand in heaven.
R.21: There {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is far above every ruler and authority, every power and lord, and every name anyone can call on. He is above them, not only in this age but also in the age to come.

decisions.choice: because of this: because of all God has done for them in Christ (verses 3-14)
alternatives: because of their faith and love only
decisions.reason: Διὰ τοῦτο looks back to the blessings just praised, and especially to the readers' share in them (verses 13-14). Hearing of their faith and love, Paul gives thanks and prays.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "and the love toward all the holy ones"
alternatives: "your faith in the Lord Jesus and toward all the holy ones", without "love"
decisions.reason: Several of the earliest manuscripts, among them P46 and Codex Vaticanus, do not have τὴν ἀγάπην, which leaves faith directed both to Jesus and to the holy ones. The words may have dropped out when a copyist's eye skipped between the two forms of the article. Faith and love together are Paul's usual pair (Colossians 1:4). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of wisdom and revelation: the Holy Spirit, who gives wisdom and reveals God
alternatives: a spirit of wisdom: a wise and perceptive frame of mind
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα has no article and could mean a disposition ("a spirit of wisdom"). But only God's Spirit gives revelation, and Isaiah 11:2 promises the Messiah "the Spirit of wisdom". The readers have already received the Spirit (1:13), so Paul is praying that the Spirit will do this work in them, not that they receive him for the first time. On either reading the wisdom comes from God.

decisions.choice: the Father of glory: the glorious Father, to whom glory belongs
decisions.reason: Like "the glory of his grace" (verse 6), the phrase describes: the Father is glorious (compare "the God of glory", Acts 7:2; Psalm 29:3).

decisions.choice: in the knowledge of him: so that they come to know God more fully
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ most naturally refers to God, the subject of the sentence. ἐπιγνώσει is knowledge that is personal and full, not information only (as in Colossians 1:9-10).

decisions.choice: the eyes of the heart enlightened: inner understanding opened, so that one sees what God has done
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the center of thought and will, not only of feeling. Light for the eyes of the heart is understanding given by God (Psalm 19:9; 2 Corinthians 4:6). The participle describes the state Paul prays for, as part of the gift of verse 17.

decisions.choice: three things to know: the hope of his call, the riches of his inheritance, the greatness of his power
decisions.reason: The three questions each begin with τίς or τί ("what"). The first looks back to God's call, the second to what he will gain in his people, the third to his power now at work.

decisions.choice: the hope of his calling: the hope God gave them when he called them
decisions.reason: God's call brings a sure hope with it (4:4, "one hope of your calling"): the inheritance and the final redemption of verse 14.

decisions.choice: his inheritance in the holy ones: God's own inheritance, which is his people
alternatives: the inheritance God gives, which his people share
decisions.reason: κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ is "his", God's, inheritance. In the Old Testament Israel is the Lord's inheritance (Deuteronomy 9:29; 32:9), and verses 11 and 14 have spoken of God's people as his portion and his possession. The other reading takes it as the inheritance God gives, to be shared among his holy people (Colossians 1:12). Both are taught in Scripture; the question is which Paul means here.

decisions.choice: his power beyond all measure: Paul heaps up four words for strength to stress how great it is
decisions.reason: ὑπερβάλλον means "surpassing". Paul adds δυνάμεως, ἐνέργειαν, κράτους and ἰσχύος: power, working, might, strength. The words overlap; together they say that no power is greater than the one at work for believers.

decisions.choice: seated at his right hand: the place of honor and rule, as promised in Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (Psalm 110:1) is applied to Christ's exaltation again and again in the New Testament (Mark 12:36; Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13). Verse 22 goes on with a related psalm.

decisions.choice: rule, authority, power, lordship: ranks of unseen spiritual powers, and every other power that has a name
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of the time named ranks of angels and spirits with words like these. In Ephesians the rulers and authorities are in the heavenly places (3:10) and include powers hostile to God's people (6:12); Colossians 1:16 and 2:10 use the same terms. "Every name that is named" takes in any power anyone could name or call on, as people did in prayers and spells (Acts 19:13-19 shows such practice in Ephesus).

decisions.choice: this age and the age to come: the present time and the new age God will bring
decisions.reason: Jewish teaching divided history into the present age and the age to come (Matthew 12:32). Christ's rule over every power holds now and will hold in the age to come.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}" in verse 20; {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of wisdom and revelation
alternatives: a spirit of wisdom and revelation
decisions.reason: All three levels follow m3. Literal brackets "the", since the Greek has no article.

decisions.choice: thanking God for you
decisions.reason: Thanks are given to God; Balanced and Readable say so, as Colossians 1:3 does.

decisions.choice: how rich and glorious an inheritance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people (B); how glorious and precious {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people are to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: they are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own treasured inheritance (R)
alternatives: the riches of his glorious inheritance among the saints
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m9.

decisions.choice: every ruler and authority, every power and dominion (B); every ruler and authority, every power and lord (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Colossians 1:16. "Ruler and authority" is kept at every level, as in the Ephesians word list, so that 3:10 and 6:12 can be traced back here.

decisions.choice: in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer phrase from the Ephesians word list.

decisions.choice: so that you will understand three things; Nothing can compare with it; God gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the place of honor at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand
alternatives: so that you may know what is the hope...; surpassing greatness; seated him at his right hand
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences, says plainly that there are three things to know (m7), and explains "surpassing" and "right hand" (m10, m11).

decisions.choice: every name anyone can call on
decisions.reason: Readable says what naming a power meant (m12).

records.heading: Paul prays that they may know God's power

records.source: καὶ πάντα ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν κεφαλὴν ὑπὲρ πάντα τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἥτις ἐστὶν τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν πληρουμένου.
records.gloss: And all things he subjected under the feet of him, and him he gave [as] head over all things to the church, \v 23 which is the body of him, the fullness of the [one] the all things in all filling.
pieces: God has put all things under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the church to be head over all things.
The church is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body. It is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness, filled by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who fills everything in every place and every way.

L.22: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} subjected all things under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] head over all things to the church,
L.23: which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, the fullness of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} who fills all things in all.

R.22: God has put everything under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over all things. God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} head over all things, and has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a gift to the church.
R.23: The church is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, and it is full of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He fills all things completely.

decisions.choice: he put all things under his feet: Psalm 8:7, applied to Christ
decisions.reason: Psalm 8:7 says of humankind, "you have put all things under his feet". Paul changes "you" to "he" and applies the line to Christ, the man in whom God's purpose for humankind is fulfilled, as 1 Corinthians 15:27 and Hebrews 2:6-9 also do. With Psalm 110:1 in verse 20, it pictures Christ ruling over every power.

decisions.choice: God gave Christ, head over all things, to the church
alternatives: God made Christ head over all things for the sake of the church
God made Christ head of the church
decisions.reason: τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ is the one Christ is given to: the head over all things is God's gift to the church, and rules for its good. That he is also head of the church follows in verse 23 (and 4:15; 5:23), but here "over all things" is the point.

decisions.choice: head: the one who rules over all, and the body's source of life
decisions.reason: κεφαλὴν here means authority "over all things"; with "his body" in verse 23 it also brings in the picture of the head that holds the body together and gives it growth (4:15-16; Colossians 1:18; 2:19).

decisions.choice: church: God's people as a whole, everywhere
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ is the gathered people. In Ephesians it always means the whole church, Christ's one body (3:10, 21; 5:23-32).

decisions.choice: the church is Christ's fullness: filled by him and with him
alternatives: the church completes Christ, who would be incomplete without it
"the fullness" describes Christ, not the church
decisions.reason: πλήρωμα stands next to "his body" and most naturally describes the church. In Ephesians the church is what Christ fills: Paul prays they will be filled to all the fullness of God (3:19), and Christ gives gifts to bring the church to "the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ" (4:13). Colossians 2:9-10 says the same: in Christ dwells all the fullness, and in him believers have been filled. That Christ needs the church to complete him is possible grammatically but fits the rest of the letter poorly.

decisions.choice: who fills all things in every way: Christ is the one who fills
alternatives: who is being filled in every way (by God, or by the church)
decisions.reason: πληρουμένου can be passive ("being filled") or middle with an active sense ("filling"). The object τὰ πάντα shows that he fills something, and 4:10 says Christ ascended "so that he might fill all things". ἐν πᾶσιν means "in every way" or "in all places".

decisions.choice: God has put all things under the feet of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
alternatives: he subjected all things under his feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, who subjects, and Christ, under whose feet all things are put, since the pronouns alone would be unclear.

decisions.choice: so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules over all things; has given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a gift to the church
alternatives: gave him as head over all things to the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what the psalm picture means and makes plain that Christ is given to the church (m2).

decisions.choice: it is full of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He fills all things completely
alternatives: the fullness of him who fills all in all
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m5 and m6 in plain words, using "full" and "fill" as the Ephesians word list allows.
